question: The type of carbohydrate predominantly found in potatoes is ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary carbohydrate found in **potatoes** is **starch**.
 
• Starch is a type of **complex carbohydrate** composed of numerous glucose units.
 
• It serves as a significant **energy source** for the human body.
 
• In potatoes, starch is stored in the form of **granules** within the cells.
 
• Starch in potatoes is utilized in various **culinary applications**, including baking, boiling, and frying.
 
• It is also used in the **food industry** for making products like **potato starch** and **potato flour**.
 
• Potato starch has the unique property of being a **thickening agent** in soups, sauces, and other dishes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sugar**__

 __
 
• **Sugar** is a simple carbohydrate that is rapidly absorbed by the body to provide quick energy.
 
• It is not the predominant carbohydrate in potatoes, though small amounts can be found.
 
• Examples of sugar include **sucrose, glucose, and fructose**.
 
 
 
• **Glucose**__
 __
 
• **Glucose** is a simple sugar and a key source of energy for cells.
 
• While glucose is a component of starch, it is not found in large amounts in its free form in potatoes.
 
 
 
• **Fructose**__
 
 
• **Fructose** is another type of simple sugar, commonly found in fruits.
 
• It is not the main carbohydrate in potatoes.
